transcript.text: Hi everyone, thanks for being here. As you know, we're planning to plant a living memorial for our grandmother in the shared backyard, and I'm coordinating the tree choice, planting arrangements, and care plan. We have one Saturday morning set aside for planting, and we want the memorial to be easy for relatives to visit. The backyard has an open east lawn, a shaded north wall, and an existing paved path. Before I finalize anything, I'd like to hear from each of you — what preferences do you have, what practical constraints should I know about, and has anyone gathered any information that might help us choose the right tree and location?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I actually have something important to share. I found the last note Grandma wrote about the memorial. She specifically wanted a native serviceberry planted at the east edge of the lawn, with no plaque attached to the trunk. I think we should honor that wish.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I have some useful info — I called the local nursery and found out that the reserved serviceberry will be ready for pickup only on Saturday, April 17, 2027. They'll hold it until noon that day. I haven't had a chance to share this with anyone yet, but it seems like it could work well with our Saturday morning planting plan.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I have some useful information too. I asked an arborist to review a photo of our yard, and they recommended that we plant the serviceberry at least 2 meters away from the paved path. They also advised watering it twice a week for the first eight weeks after planting.
transcript.speaker: A4
